target_customer: Engineering and ops teams at companies using Salesforce, Airtable or Notion alongside a backend database
problem: Ops teams edit data in business tools while engineers use the database, and keeping the two in sync required costly or hand-built pipelines.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for managed sync pipelines

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable bidirectional sync with conflict handling and API rate limits across SaaS tools is hard but well understood.

defensibility.rationale: Once wired into a production database, sync has some stickiness, but competitors like Whalesync and Stacksync offered similar sync.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; LinkedIn reports Rippling acquired the company, with no date or terms found.

market_need_then: Heroku Connect was costly (the company cited above $50k a year) and tied to Heroku Postgres, creating demand for cheaper hosting-agnostic sync.

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN and Show HN posts drew little engagement (Show HN had 6 points and no comments).

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with many products; search for the brand returned mostly unrelated results and no brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: Bracket was a three person YC W22 team selling two-way sync between Salesforce, Airtable and databases as a cheaper Heroku Connect alternative. Funding figures from aggregators conflict ($1M to $2.5M) and none are verified. It is listed as acquired, with Rippling named only by its LinkedIn page, and no deal date or price exists, so the soft landing label is an inference from team size and silence rather than a sourced fact.
notes: Acquirer Rippling comes from a single LinkedIn page; unverified, no date. Funding totals ($1.0M VCBacked, $2.0M AlphaGrowth, $2.5M CB Insights listing a Los Angeles company) conflict and may mix companies, so no rounds recorded. The Launch HN and Show HN posts appear to date from 2023, after the batch. No dated competitor source near the batch found: reverse ETL searches returned only current vendor pages. The YC page lists app.usebracket.com; website field in the directory was empty and was not fetched separately.
